title: 2022 HMMT February Algebra and Number Theory Problem 1
statement: Positive integers \(a, b\), and \(c\) are all powers of \(k\) for some positive integer \(k\). It is known that the equation \(a x^{2}-b x+c=0\) has exactly one real solution \(r\), and this value \(r\) is less than 100 . Compute the maximum possible value of \(r\).

solutions.text: Note that for there to be exactly one solution, the discriminant must be 0 , so \(b^{2}-4 a c=0\). Thus, \(b\) is even, so \(k=2\). Since \(r=\frac{b}{2 a}\), then \(r\) is also a power of 2 , and the largest power of 2 less than 100 is 64 . This is achieved by \((x-64)^{2}=x^{2}-128 x+4096\).
